summary: Built in 1921 on State Game Lands #91 and staffed for decades, including by a teenage watcher known as "Honey" from 1922; whether it still stands after a reported 2018 replacement is unresolved.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree on current status: a 2018 StoryMap entry implies a tower still stands (replaced that year), while a lookout register marks it "Removed" with no date. The StoryMap's own text also gives two conflicting heights for the current tower ("60 foot" and "80 feet" in the same sentence), so no height is recorded here.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters

events.note: Aermotor Windmill Company tower erected; later record attributes the district to the Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters.
A fifteen-year-old watcher known locally as "Honey" was appointed by district forester R. Lynn Emmerick.
Last staffing on record: watcher Peter Dubinsky, operating from a site a local paper placed on the "Conlon Estate" near Bear Creek.
StoryMap states the original tower was replaced this year; conflicts with a separate source marking the tower removed.

corrections.evidence: A 1949 newspaper item puts the tower at 1,921 feet above sea level; a 1948 item puts it at 1,931 feet (both quoted on the lookout register).

notes_for_editor: Status conflict is real and unresolved from these two sources alone: StoryMap implies a current tower (replaced 2018), the lookout register says "Removed" with no date. The StoryMap's own text is internally inconsistent, calling the tower both '60 foot' and '80 feet' in the same sentence. Newspaper elevation figures also vary by 10 feet (1,921 vs 1,931 ft) between 1949 and 1948 clippings -- likely OCR/reporting noise, not a real change. A primary PA DCNR or Bureau of Forestry record, if available, would help settle current status.
